findings.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:9–11 unconditionally accesses result row [0], causing the migration to abort before fallback when embed_category is unset or references a deleted category, blocking installation or upgrade.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:26 copies legacy hosts without normalization, so URL values such as https://example.com/path fail hostname-only lookup and break embedding after upgrade.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 limits top-level domains to five letters, rejecting valid hosts such as example.museum and example.technology and preventing administrators from adding or editing their embedding relationships.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14–17 accepts hosts containing ports but compares stored values against uri.host, which excludes ports, causing authorization to fail for saved hosts such as example.com:3000.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 limits top-level domains to five letters, rejecting valid hosts such as example.museum and example.technology and preventing administrators from adding or editing their embedding relationships.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. This would reject valid TLDs like '.museum' (6 chars), '.technology' (10 chars), and many other newer gTLDs. This is a real validation bug that would prevent administrators from adding legitimate embeddable hosts with longer TLDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14–17 accepts hosts containing ports but compares stored values against uri.host, which excludes ports, causing authorization to fail for saved hosts such as example.com:3000.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the EmbeddableHost model, the validation regex allows ports: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/i`. The before_validation strips the protocol and path but keeps the port in the host field. In `record_for_host`, it extracts `uri.host` which does NOT include the port (URI parsing separates host and port). So if you save 'example.com:3000', the stored host is 'example.com:3000', but when checking, `uri.host` returns just 'example.com'. The comparison `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` would compare 'example.com' against 'example.com:3000', which would fail. This is a real bug - hosts with ports would be saved but never match during authorization checks.
